title: 1 in 4 Americans have hidden in the bathroom to survive the holidays

# Press releases


# 1 in 4 Americans have hidden in the bathroom to survive the holidays


Nov 19, 2026


- [Photos (1)](https://zillow.mediaroom.com/2026-11-19-1-in-4-Americans-have-hidden-in-the-bathroom-to-survive-the-holidays#assets_28775_138135-135)


# Holiday-Hosting_Nov-2026


Thursday, November 19, 2026 (8:00am)


Zillow's holiday hosting survival kit


- [Download Hi-Res](https://mmx.prnewswire.com/media/MS2039244/Holiday-Hosting_Nov-2026.jpg?id=OA3089994&p=original)


[CLOSE](https://zillow.mediaroom.com/2026-11-19-1-in-4-Americans-have-hidden-in-the-bathroom-to-survive-the-holidays#Closed)


*New Zillow survey finds cleaning, in-laws and cramped quarters strain holiday hosts*


- Two-thirds of Americans have hidden from their holiday guests for a few minutes of peace.
- Cleaning, not cooking, is the most stressful part of hosting a holiday meal, according to nearly half of Americans (48%).
- The three-night rule: 70% of Americans would ideally have overnight holiday guests stay three nights or fewer.
- Still, 50% love holiday meal hosting, and 71% want a table packed with family and friends.


SEATTLE


, Nov. 19, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- For nearly 1 in 4 Americans, the best seat in the house during the holidays may be behind a locked bathroom door (23%). A new Zillow® survey conducted by The Harris Poll finds that, whether it's in a bathroom, a bedroom or a car, two-thirds of Americans (66%) admit to hiding somewhere to get a few minutes of peace away from their holiday guests. Hosting comes with plenty of pressure, from cleaning and cooking to difficult family members and homes that were not built for a crowd. But Zillow's survey also finds that despite the stress, half of Americans say they love hosting holiday meals, and most (71%) dream of a full table of family and friends.


A lot of work comes with hosting a crowd. Nearly half of Americans (48%) put cleaning among the most stressful parts of hosting a holiday meal, ahead of cooking (33%), having enough room for everyone to sit (28%) and the cost (27%). Family dynamics can elevate the stress. More than one-quarter of Americans say their parents or in-laws are the most stressful holiday guests (26%), followed by siblings and/or their partners (21%).


Nearly 3 in 4 Americans (73%) say some aspect of their home causes them stress when hosting a holiday meal, most often from not having enough seats or a table that's big enough (32%) or not having enough counter space (29%). It's no wonder 82% of holiday meal hosts have set up tables somewhere other than the dining room.


Overnight guests add to the agita. More than 4 in 5 Americans (81%) have welcomed them during the holidays, and among those hosts, 44% have had someone sleep on the couch, 35% on an air mattress or cot, and 16% have given up their own bed. Most Americans (70%) agree that three nights or fewer is the ideal length of stay for an overnight guest during the holidays.


Some have tried to get out of holiday hosting altogether. Twenty percent of Americans have blamed their home's size, and about 1 in 10 (11%) have considered moving farther away from family. Others wish they had a home better suited to the occasion: 17% of Americans have considered converting unused space into a guest room, and 16% have considered buying a home with more bedrooms to make it easier to host overnight guests during the holidays.


"The holidays can put a home to the ultimate test, and this survey shows how much our homes shape the way we celebrate," said Amanda Pendleton, Zillow's home trends expert. "Too few seats, a cramped kitchen or no spare bedroom can turn a favorite tradition into a frenzied one. It's no surprise many Americans have thought about moving or adding a room to their home when space is what stands between them and the holiday they picture."


Even in tight quarters, almost no one wants to skip the holidays at home. Nine in 10 Americans (91%) have hosted a holiday meal, and half (50%) say they love hosting. Only 5% openly hate hosting, and just 11% say they host out of obligation but secretly hate it. About 7 in 10 (71%) would ideally host a wide circle of guests for a holiday meal, including immediate and extended family or a mix of family and friends. And for nearly 1 in 4 Americans, the more guests the merrier; 24% would welcome 13 or more guests to their holiday table.


**Methodology**


This survey was conducted online within the United States by The Harris Poll on behalf of Zillow November 11–13, 2026 among 2,006 U.S. adults ages 18 and older. The sampling precision of Harris online polls is measured by using a Bayesian credible interval. For this study, the sample data is accurate to within +/- 2.7 percentage points using a 95% confidence level. This credible interval will be wider among subsets of the surveyed population of interest. For complete survey methodology, including weighting variables and subgroup sample sizes, please contactpress@zillow.com .
